name: Lab safety
description: Incident management for research laboratories: exposure and incident reports, notification matrices with clocks, inventory reconciliations, freezer alarms and access logs. Exercises concern what an organization decides and whom it tells. The toolkit carries guardrails that keep agent handling, production and modification detail out of every product.
outsideParties: the Federal Select Agent Program (CDC Division of Regulatory Science and Compliance or APHIS Agricultural Select Agent Services)
the NIH Office of Science Policy
the local fire department and hazmat team
campus police and local law enforcement
the vendor of the monitoring or inventory system

advisorRoles.name: Biosafety officer (advisor)
advisorRoles.description: Explains what the biosafety program would do and which notifications and deadlines apply; never gives agent handling detail.

metrics.label: Select agent notifications: immediate notices and the Form 3 worksheet within 7 calendar days (exercise window of 60 minutes for 'immediately')
Institution and NIH notifications: biosafety officer in 24 hours, IBC chair in 3 days, sponsor in 7 days, NIH in 30 days

metrics.label: Exposure response: stop-work within the protocol time of the exposure report
Exposure response: worker sent for medical evaluation within the protocol time
Exposure follow-up: people in and near the room reached within the designer's target
Samples saved: share moved to backup before the designer's limit
Samples moved before the designer's limit (degrees C above the limit)
Data recovery: systems restored and hours of work lost
Lab, EHS, compliance and communications messages agree on the key facts

decisionForms.label: Classify the incident
decisionForms.description: Decide what kind of incident this is and on what basis; the classification decides which notifications are due.

fields.label: Classification
choices: Reportable to NIH through the IBC
Internal incident with no external report

decisionForms.label: Notify a party
decisionForms.description: Record who was told, how and when. The time is the time of the notification.

decisionForms.label: Stop work in an area
decisionForms.description: Order work to stop in a room or suite until a named condition is met.

decisionForms.label: Send a worker for medical evaluation
decisionForms.description: Refer a worker by code, never by a real name.

decisionForms.label: Restrict a worker
decisionForms.description: Set a work restriction after an incident.

decisionForms.label: Move samples to backup
decisionForms.description: Move a group of samples to a backup unit. If only some can move, give a count; the register order decides which.

fields.label: How many (leave empty for the whole group)

decisionForms.label: Activate the incident response plan
decisionForms.description: Activate the entity's incident response plan.

decisionForms.label: Order an evacuation
decisionForms.description: Order people out of a room, wing or building.

decisionForms.label: Submit a written report
decisionForms.description: Record which written report was submitted and when. Exercise worksheets are not official forms.

decisionForms.label: Brief the institutional official
decisionForms.description: Record a briefing of the institutional official or vice president for research.

decisionForms.label: Issue a statement
decisionForms.description: Release a statement. Keep it to what the organization decided and whom it told.

decisionForms.label: Restore a system from backup
decisionForms.description: Restore a research system. The time reads the backup series to show how much work was lost.

glossary.definition: biosafety officer: classifies incidents, checks containment, refers exposed workers for medical evaluation, reports to the IBC.
responsible official and alternate of a select agent registration: decide notice to the Federal Select Agent Program and the written report.
institutional biosafety committee: reviews incidents; reports to NIH for recombinant or synthetic nucleic acid research.
APHIS/CDC report of theft, loss or release, due 7 calendar days after discovery. Exercise worksheets are never the official form.
a registered entity's written plan (42 CFR 73.14), drilled at least annually and reviewed after every drill, exercise or incident.
how the plan was tested, problems found, corrective actions and participants.

productConventions: Give every incident product a report number (LI-2026-0142), the date and time of discovery and the room.
Write times in 24-hour local time with the date, and a deadline with its basis: immediately, within 24 hours of awareness, within 7 calendar days of discovery, within 30 days.

Mark worksheets 'Exercise worksheet, not the official form'. Name an agent only as a generic class ('a select agent', 'a Risk Group 2 bacterium') or from the designer's reviewed list, with its biosafety level and nothing else.
Write each notification as who, how and when, next to its deadline.
realismRules: An inventory discrepancy is usually a records problem: a transfer logged in one place only, an unsigned destruction, a mislabeled box. Show the search before the conclusion.

Select agent theft or loss, and a release causing occupational exposure, are reported immediately to CDC or APHIS (theft or loss also to law enforcement); the Form 3 is due within 7 calendar days of discovery.

NIH Guidelines: IBC reports significant problems and accidents to NIH within 30 days; an overt exposure at BL2, or an overt or potential exposure at BL3 or BL4, is reported immediately. The draft NIH policy NOT-OD-26-112 (August 19, 2026) proposes 24 hours; call it a draft.
An institution may set shorter deadlines; the stricter rule governs. Say which one applies.
A freezer alarm fails through a changed call-out number, a silenced alarm or an offline sensor. Viability windows are the designer's exercise parameters, never biology.
Never describe methods, protocols, doses, concentrations, strain names or the making, growing, changing or spreading of anything biological. Keep the story on people, records, clocks and messages.

criticalTasks: Activate the incident response plan and name who holds each role, including the alternate responsible official when the first is absent.
Coordinate the biosafety office, the laboratory, facilities, security and occupational health under one picture of the incident.
Decide who orders stop-work and what lifts it.

ids: Incident response plan: roles and lines of authority

criticalTasks: Make each required notification to the right party, by the right route, inside its deadline.
Keep the written report, the committee minutes and the notice to the sponsor consistent.
Keep a working call-out path when the alarm or phone tree fails.

ids: Notification of theft, loss or release

criticalTasks: Issue a statement that matches the record and says nothing the record does not support.
Tell staff, students, the sponsor and neighbors what they need, in that order of need.
Never name an agent or give a handling detail in public material.
Reconcile the inventory against transfers, destruction logs and the audit trail before concluding loss.
Establish who was in the room, who was exposed and who has been reached.
Establish what was lost, moved or restored, and what remains at risk.
Stop work, secure the area and refer exposed workers for evaluation within the protocol times.
Brief emergency responders on facility hazards only and keep them out of restricted rooms without the biosafety officer.
Return rooms to use in order, on stated conditions, with a sign-off.

exerciseTags.label: Select agent incident response plan drill
exerciseTags.description: A registered entity's annual test of its written incident response plan: theft, loss or release, inventory discrepancies, security breaches, severe weather, workplace violence, fire and power outages.
objectives: Test the roles and lines of authority in the incident response plan.
Test immediate notification and the written report deadline.
Test coordination with local emergency responders.
exerciseTags.participants: The responsible official and alternate, the biosafety officer, laboratory staff, facilities and security, and local responders as the plan names them.
exerciseTags.frequency: At least annually, and the plan is reviewed again after any drill, exercise or incident
notes: Drills or exercises must be conducted at least annually to test and evaluate the effectiveness of the plan.
Follow your registration and the program's current guidance; this record is an exercise aid.

drillRecord.reviewPrompt: Review the incident response plan now and revise it as necessary. The regulation requires a review after any drill, exercise or incident; record the review and the date.
